items.title: Spinodal-controlled freeze-out and nucleation at the first-order superfluid-supersolid transition of a dipolar gas
items.summary: Dipolar quantum gases in elongated traps become supersolid through a transition that is continuous at intermediate density but first order at low and high density; at the continuous point, ramps of the scattering length follow Kibble--Zurek scaling. We study ramps across the first-order superfluid--supersolid transition of $^{164}$Dy in an infinite tube using the three-dimensional extended Gross--Pitaevskii equation with truncated-Wigner noise. With quantum noise only, the uniform superfluid survives the metastable window and transforms after its spinodal, where the roton softens. For onsets occurring during the linear ramp, the delay measured from this spinodal has a fitted exponent $\zeta = 0.36 \pm 0.02$, close to the continuous-transition result and the mean-field value $1/3$. The quoted uncertainty combines statistical and systematic sensitivities. Reverse ramps show a comparable delay beyond the fold of the crystal branch, producing dynamical hysteresis. Initial thermal noise with nominal temperatures of 2.5--10 nK produces crystalline regions inside the metastable window during holds, with faster nucleation closer to the spinodal and at higher initial temperature. Without a heat bath these effective rates depend on preparation: ramps crossing the window at the same rate nucleate early in 2 of 32 or 11 of 16 realizations depending on their starting point. A crossover time inferred from hold rates is therefore an estimate, not a measured boundary for the ramp protocol. At low density, slower ramps select larger spacings in a crystal of separated droplets, and droplets survive far above the transition on reverse ramps.

items.title: Surface scalar plasmons on curved interfaces: a venue for analogue gravity
items.summary: We investigate whether the geometry of a curved conductor--dielectric interface can modify the effective mass and propagation of scalar surface plasmons (SSPs). In the hydrodynamic limit, we describe SSPs as density perturbations in a semiclassical jellium electron gas. Using a thin--layer dimensional reduction procedure, we derive a massive Klein--Gordon equation for SSPs on the curved interface with a geometric potential. We find that under specific conditions, the geometric potential allows SSP propagation with a vanishing effective mass. We then apply the formalism to a well known analogue black hole configuration, determining the corresponding quasinormal mode frequencies. Our results show that interface curvature provides a geometric handle on plasmon propagation and localization, suggesting new possibilities for plasmon transport and analogue gravity experiments with surface plasmons.

items.title: Cooper Instability of a Magnetic Wigner Crystal
items.summary: Recent scanning tunneling microscopy has directly imaged electronic crystals in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, and magnetotransport measurements suggest that superconductivity and charge-density-wave order emerge from a common spin-valley-polarized ferromagnetic metal at nearby carrier densities. Motivated by these observations, we ask whether collective modes in a magnetic Wigner crystal can mediate pairing in this setting. We address this question by studying the Cooper problem for two electrons in the first conduction band of the Wigner crystal. Unlike conventional phonon-mediated pairing, the collective mode (boson) energies and single-particle (fermion) dispersion are comparable scales controlled by the electron density, leaving no small parameter for an adiabatic expansion. Moreover, because the magnetic Wigner crystal is not time-reversal invariant, the usual Cooper logarithmic divergence in the pairing susceptibility is absent, so the attraction must exceed a finite threshold for pairing to occur. These unusual features motivate a numerical experiment to see whether the crystal's own vibrations can bind electrons. We obtain the crystalline ground state and its collective mode spectrum within Hartree--Fock and time-dependent Hartree--Fock approximation, and derive the electron--phonon Hamiltonian using the quasiboson approximation. Solving the resulting two-electron problem, we find that phonon-mediated attraction exceeds the pairing threshold, with chiral $p$-wave pairing as the leading instability. Within these approximations, we show that collective modes of a Wigner crystal can indeed favor chiral pairing despite broken time-reversal symmetry. Our results provide an encouraging starting point for developing a full many-body theory to study electronic crystallization and superconductivity.

items.title: Why has PET glycolysis remained difficult to industrialize despite decades of optimization?
items.summary: Classical PET glycolysis struggles with industrial scale-up due to a research paradigm defect: uncoupled reaction optimization that ignores system-level engineering entropy. By establishing a governing reference frame, Scientific Reasoning Units (SRUs) and human-AI collaborative discovery in this article, we present a Three-Step Synergistic Reinforcement Paradigm addressing the triple failure modes of traditional systems-mass-transfer collapse, viscosity deadlock, and side-reaction accumulation. By integrating twin-screw controlled shearing, solid-state micro-homogenization, and deep depolymerization (2:1 EG/Oligomer ratio), we achieve an ultrafast kinetic regime. BHET yields surge to 80% to 95% within 10 minutes, eliminating multi-hour thermal bottlenecks and delivering an economically viable framework for closed-loop polyester recycling.

items.title: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78617-3 Plant invasions can threaten ecosystems by making plant communities less stable over time. The study shows that invasions reduce stability from local to metacommunity scales by eroding functional diversity and favoring fast-growing strategies.

items.title: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78587-6 RNA sensors have been linked to antitumor immune responses. Here, based on results of in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors propose the RNA sensor MDA5 as a regulator of immune evasion, showing that its targeting induces immunogenic cell death and anti tumor immunity.

items.title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78616-4 A method developed to directly measure fungal melanin in soil, reveals a strong link between melanin and soil carbon and providing evidence for its role in long-term carbon stabilization

items.title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78555-0 Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.

items.title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78598-3 Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets.

items.title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78648-w Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery.

items.title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78575-w Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report alternating Ni/NiMoO₄ heterostructures that promote hydrogen evolution and sustain durable high-current electrolysis.

items.title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78603-9 This study shows that unequal changes in bloom duration between hemispheres contribute to contrasting high-latitude ocean chlorophyll trends, linking asymmetric phytoplankton phenology to marine ecosystem changes under climate warming.

items.title: Unveiling the Bose-Einstein condensate-droplet crossover with Rayleigh superradiant scattering
authors: Mithilesh K. Parit, Mingchen Huang, Ziting Chen, Yifei He, Haoting Zhen, and Gyu-Boong Jo
items.summary: Light scattering plays an essential role in uncovering the properties of quantum states through light-matter interactions. Here, we explore the crossover from Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) to droplets in a dipolar ${}^{166}$Er gas by employing superradiant light scattering as both a probing and con…

items.title: Emergence of nonequilibrium Lieb excitations in periodically-driven strongly-interacting bosons
authors: Hoshu Hiyane, Giedrius Žlabys, Thomas Busch, and Shohei Watabe
items.summary: The time-averaged spectral function plays a central role in studying the Floquet properties of the many-body fermionic systems. Here, we study the time-averaged spectral function of the periodically driven bosonic systems by providing an exact and rigorous analysis in the strongly interacting one-di…

items.title: Ab initio complex Langevin computation of the roton gap for a dipolar Bose condensate
authors: Philipp Heinen, Wyatt Kirkby, Lauriane Chomaz, and Thomas Gasenzer
items.summary: We compute from first principles the dispersion relation of a finite-temperature dipolar Bose gas near the roton instability. Using a field-theoretic Complex Langevin (CL) approach, we access experimentally relevant atom numbers. We determine the roton excitation gap as a function of the s-wave scat…

items.title: Metal-organic frameworks for separation of organic compounds in liquid phase
items.summary: Abstract Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), showing exceptional tunability in composition, topology and pore environment, hold unique promise to address this challenge. This review surveys recent progress in studies of MOFs for the selective extraction and purification of organic substrates in liquid phase, with a focus on elucidating the mechanism of selectivity. Function-directed design principles, encompassing tailored bonding interactions, programmable supramolecular environments and pore-confinement effects, are discussed as enabling precise control over transport processes. These concepts are examined across key application domains, including removal of pollutants in water treatment, the separation of structurally similar hydrocarbons in petrochemical refinery and the selective discrimination of daily pharmaceuticals. Opportunities for the next generation of MOF-based sorbents are outlined, highlighting challenges associated with scalability and long-term operational stability, and the growing roles of artificial intelligence (AI)-guided discovery in developing sustainable separation technologies are further projected.

items.title: An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor
items.summary: Scattering of quasiparticles provides direct access to the interactions that govern strongly correlated systems. In this work, we realize the quasiparticle scattering experiment of the Fermi-Hubbard model on a digital quantum processor by colliding a doublon and a holon in the half-filled chain of 21 sites encoded on 42 qubits of the ibm_boston processor. For the first time, we measure the transmission probability of quasiparticles of the Hubbard model on quantum hardware, which agrees with the Bethe-ansatz scattering matrix without free parameters. Beyond the scattering probabilities, the collision generates entanglement by superposing the transmitted and reflected components, which we infer from the particle-number fluctuation. In sharp contrast, a control collision between two doublons shows neither the interaction dependence nor the number fluctuation, as expected for indistinguishable particles. Our work demonstrates that the ability to create quasiparticles of a chosen flavor on demand and program their motion and interactions makes a digital quantum processor a new experimental toolset for probing the entanglement structure generated by quasiparticle scattering.

items.title: A Warped Born Rule Turns an Observer into a Maxwell's Demon
items.summary: Quantum mechanics seems to be an incredibly delicate theory. Slight alterations to nearly any part of its structure can lead to huge qualitative differences and wildly unphysical predictions. Here, we explore the many-body consequences of replacing the Born rule $p(m)\propto\|P_m|ψ\rangle|^2$ by a warped rule $p_b(m)\propto\|P_m|ψ\rangle\|^{2b}$. Specifically, in systems with conserved particle number, evolution punctuated by repeated local particle observations acquires a probabilistic bias over measurement histories with an effect controlled by the sign of $b-1$. For $b>1$, this bias generically drives the gas to collect into nearly frozen configurations. Similar to the action of Maxwell's demon, the simple act of observation seems to extract entropy from a closed system. For $b<1$, the bias is reversed, generically scouring out long-wavelength fluctuations to produce a hyperuniform gas. We study this effect in a one-dimensional quantum gas, where these two phases are derived analytically for a particular measurement scheme and corroborated numerically for more general procedures with discrete-time projective-measurement circuit models using matrix product state simulations. We additionally discuss how this bias manifests in a common technique that often employs this warped rule, the ``replica trick,'' implying qualitative differences between finite-replica and replica-limit calculations.

items.title: Domain-wall circulation gating and pinning via compositional engineering of cylindrical nanowires
items.summary: Spintronic devices based on cylindrical magnetic nanowires have been proposed as a route toward three-dimensional information storage and processing by harnessing the controlled motion of domain walls (DWs). In this geometry, the Bloch-point wall (BPW) is the characteristic DW type. It features a curling of magnetization around a Bloch Point singularity, a topology that has been predicted to enable propagation at high speed without undergoing a Walker breakdown. We demonstrate that compositional modulations of larger magnetization, which host spontaneous curling states while the rest of the wire remains axial, fulfil a dual role: they act as deterministic pinning sites and as active gates for BPW circulation. Combining magnetic transmission X-ray microscopy and micromagnetic simulations, we reveal that DW-modulation interactions are the result of a superposition of long-range magnetostatic repulsion and short-range, circulation-dependent exchange contributions: parallel circulation produces an attractive well, while opposite circulation generates a repulsive barrier. This results in DW pinning at or near a compositional modulation. A DW's internal circulation can be inverted upon traversing a modulation, enabling on-demand switching of its circulation state. This dual mechanism demonstrates that both DW position and circulation can be tuned in a controlled manner, with potential implications for multistate spintronic devices.

items.title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson Volumes from the Spectral Edge of DSSYK and Supersymmetric Extensions
items.summary: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same q-deformed volumes can be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call "irrelevant" contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how q-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

items.title: Necessary conditions for benchmarking next-generation AI in materials discovery
items.summary: Current AI predicts materials by speeding up energy minimisation and training on large databases. However, scaling data generation prevents manual analysis by domain experts. If novelty is evaluated by chemical compositions or traditional representations in Crystallographic Information Files, or standard structure matchers based on manually chosen thresholds, one can easily generate millions of ``new'' compositions or files without discovering truly novel materials. This paper uses a hierarchy of crystal invariants to continuously trace and quantify structural novelty based on the new mathematical definition of a crystal structure and asymptotic guarantees for invariant descriptors. The invariant-based analysis through cascade computations on a modest computer exposes the unexpected scale of duplication in the world's largest materials databases, shown here in the high-profile case of GNoME datasets. To prevent current ``embarrassment of over-prediction'', we propose necessary conditions for next-generation AI that should be automatically enforced before claiming any new materials.

items.title: Quantum Theory of Exciton Magnetic Moment: Interaction and Topological Effects
items.summary: Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. Our formalism reveals three distinct contributions that go beyond the heuristic approaches used in the literature: a Berry-phase-corrected single-particle electron and hole moment difference, a term from envelope-function winding linked to electron-hole relative motion, and a center-of-mass correction from exciton band quantum geometry, with the latter two being completely new effects not considered in previous studies. Our ab initio calculations yield results in excellent agreement with experiment, establishing the importance of interaction and quantum geometric effects in the magnetic response of excitons.

items.title: Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
items.summary: We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$σ$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $α_σ$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.

items.title: Potential energy release rate for solids with bounded domains during evolutions involving changes to boundaries and boundary data
items.summary: We investigate the rate of change of equilibrium potential energy for nonlinear elastic solids undergoing evolutions that may involve changes in body geometry, material properties, applied tractions, and prescribed displacements. We represent such an evolution by a one-parameter family of variational problems and identify a class of these families for which the potential-energy release rate is well defined. Particular attention is given to the formulation of the potential energy at each evolution state: each constituent variational problem must yield the appropriate equilibrium state, while its equilibrium value must also correctly represent the physical change in potential energy between states. Within this framework, we derive a closed-form expression for the potential-energy release rate for solids with bounded domains, allowing for spatially nonuniform material evolution, sharp material interfaces, and evolving boundary geometry and prescribed boundary data. The expression is determined entirely by the equilibrium solution at the state under consideration and by the quantities prescribing the local evolution, so neighboring equilibrium problems need not be solved. Finally, we apply the result to the extension of a notch in a two-dimensional elastic body and show that the resulting potential-energy release rate reduces to the classical $J$-integral.

items.title: Closed analytical form of many-body free volume and thermodynamics of monodisperse hard disks
items.summary: The hard disk model is a fundamental reference system for excluded volume physics, liquid structure, and 2D ordering. Yet, despite its apparent simplicity, an analytical formulation of its thermodynamics has remained difficult because the free volume available to disks centers has a highly nontrivial many-body geometry. Here we show that this geometry admits a closed and exact representation: for any given hard disk configuration, the free volume can be analytically expressed through intersection areas of up to five exclusion disks. This provides a direct geometrical route from particle coordinates to the configurational partition function and entropy. We prove that the N disk partition function factorizes into a product of conditional free volumes and identify its two limiting asymptotic forms: the low density fluid regime controlled by extensive cavities and the high density fluid regime controlled by intensive private cells. Using the geometric measures computed from representative equilibrium particle configurations, the resulting theory reproduces the established hard disk equation of state over almost the entire density range up to close packing. At intermediate densities, the analysis reveals a mixed fluid regime in which localized caged defects provide an additional configurational entropy within the density interval preceding liquid hexatic coexistence. Finally, the five disk intersection area is shown to be a sensitive local scalar measure of hexagonal ordering, complementing the orientational order parameter and emphasizing the central role of many-body correlations.

items.title: Classification of topological phases of matter in stochastic systems
items.summary: Topological phases of matter support edge states protected from random perturbations, and the identification of the discrete non-spatial symmetries and dimensions that support such phases was systematically developed for quantum systems and analogous platforms. While topological phases were also discovered in stochastic systems and posited as mechanisms for key biochemical processes, a classification consistent with their Markovian constraints remains lacking, impeding generalization to new scenarios. To address this, we develop new methods including a new homotopy approach, real-space invariants and a redefinition of the point gap to classify both transient and steady states. We find robust transient states in two symmetry classes, no symmetry and pseudo-Hermiticity respectively, while topological steady states are expected only in systems without symmetry. We identify the dimensions with non-trivial phases and their group structure, creating a rigorous framework for predicting robust behavior in active and living matter.

items.title: Doubly Metastable Synthesis for Accelerated Quantum Materials Discovery
items.summary: New physics emerges from new materials, which in turn rely on the development of new synthesis techniques. Identifying the enlargement of metastable synthesis window as enabling for realizing novel materials, we develop diffusion-activated epitaxy, a technique which combines two metastable synthesis methods of diffusion and epitaxy. We observe that within a narrow window of investigated synthesis space we can experimentally identify the stabilization of four distinct phases, three of which show X-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy characterization data that are incompatible with the crystal structures registered in experimental and computational inorganic structure databases. These results suggest an enlarged metastable synthesis window is enabled by this synthesis approach, identifying doubly metastable synthesis as a promising method for exploration of quantum materials.

items.title: Robust Golden Ratio universality as a consequence of a circulant symmetry
items.summary: We find a robust scenario for the emergence of the Golden Ratio (GR) dynamical universality class, characterized by the dynamical exponent $z \equiv \varphi=\frac{1}{2}(1+\sqrt{5})$. Previously, its emergence required fine-tuning of system parameters. Here, the GR universality class appears generically in a wide class of Markov processes as a consequence of a global, circulant symmetry of the flux Jacobian. This symmetry leads to GR universality in systems where the total number of conservation laws is odd and larger than three. We introduce a multilane exclusion process with Bernoulli stationary measure as a minimal, parameter-free model, which features GR universality for all conserved modes, most of which are doubly degenerate. Our predictions, based on mode-coupling theory generalized to treat degenerate conserved modes, are corroborated by large-scale Monte Carlo simulations.

items.title: Guidelines for band gap opening in graphene superlattices with periodic π-vacancy distribution
items.summary: Periodic $π$-vacancies in graphene superlattices (GSLs) provide a symmetry-based route to band-gap opening in graphene by modifying the $π$-band dispersion. However, the symmetry conditions that determine whether a vacancy motif can open a band gap remain unclear. Here, we investigate periodic $π$-vacancy GSLs using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model with one $p_z$ orbital per carbon site to identify the symmetry requirements for gap opening. $π$-vacancies, representing functionalized, substituted, or missing carbon sites, are modeled as site deletions in the $π$ basis, with all hopping matrix elements to and from the deleted sites set to zero. We focus on $π$-vacancy motifs with $C_2$ and $C_3$ point-group symmetry. A $3n \times 3n$ GSL, where $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ is the integer scaling factor multiplying the honeycomb primitive-cell vectors, folds $K$ and $K'$ to $Γ$ and can therefore open a band gap. For $C_3$-type vacancies, the Dirac cones remain pinned at high-symmetry points and thus stay at $Γ$ in folded $3n$ GSLs. In contrast, $C_2$-type vacancies that reduce the global point group of the GSL to $D_{2h}$ by preserving a pair of perpendicular mirror symmetries, $σ_v \perp σ_d$, can also constrain the Dirac cones to $Γ$. When the $σ_v$ and $σ_d$ mirror planes are absent, the cones are allowed to shift away from $Γ$ to $(\pm Δq,\pm Δq)$ in the $3n$ superlattice.

items.title: Phononic Frequency Combs in Twisted Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Heterostructures from First Principles
items.summary: Phononic frequency combs are equidistant spectral ladders generated when a driven vibrational mode transfers energy to an autoparametrically excited subharmonic mode through anharmonic intermode coupling. In previous studies, the coupling strength governing this energy transfer has typically been treated as a free parameter, extracted from a fabricated device, or adopted from an earlier calculation for a specific mode pair. As a result, whether a given crystal can support a phononic frequency comb, and the drive strength required to generate it, has not been predictable a priori. Here we obtain the complete parameter set from density functional theory. Twisted bilayers of \MoSSe{} and \MoSMoSe{} at the commensurate angle $21.787^{\circ}$ adopt space group $P3$ in a 42-atom \rootseven{} moiré supercell. The second-order force constants provide the mode frequencies; the third-order constants provide the linewidths through the Boltzmann transport equation and hence the quality factors; and the same third-order tensor projected onto the phonon eigenvectors of a chosen mode pair provides the anharmonic couplings $\kt$ and $\kss$. Both bilayers constitute a mode pair within $0.8\%$ of the $2\!:\!1$ resonance with $ω_1/ω_2 = 1.9923$ in \MoSSe{} and $1.9943$ in \MoSMoSe{}. By integrating the resulting two-mode equations, both modes generate combs through a discontinuous transition: at $701\,\fth$ in \MoSSe{} the envelope variance rises from $2.1\times10^{3}$ to $1.37\times10^{4}$ and the tooth count of mode 1 from 7 to 16 within a single $5\,\fth$ increment, identifying the onset as subcritical. The spectral entropy peaks \emph{before} this jump, at $341\,\fth$. The two compounds carry comparable coupling, differing by a factor of $1.2$. However, the comb excitation threshold is set by the quality-factors of signal modes: $Q_2 = 672$ for \MoSSe{} and $Q_2 = 3844$ for \MoSMoSe{}.

items.title: Replica Transition at Measurement-Altered Ising Criticality
items.summary: Performing measurements on gapless quantum ground states can give rise to new universal phenomena, whose origins remain poorly understood even for the paradigmatic Ising critical point. Replica methods offer a natural framework to study such post-measurement ensembles, with the replica limit $Q\to 1$ describing physical Born-averaged observables. Here we show that, for the monitored critical Ising chain, the replicated post-measurement ensemble of states itself undergoes a phase transition precisely at the physically relevant replica limit $Q \to 1$, preventing standard replica treatments. We use boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) methods to explain the underlying mechanism of this transition. Our methods yield a perturbative analytic calculation of the universal $O(1)$ constant in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record, previously known only numerically. We also apply our tools to study measurement-averaged spin correlators, providing a unified description of the universal properties of measurement outcomes and post-measurement states in the critical Ising chain.

items.title: Improved screening of doped ZrO$_2$ catalysts for CO$_2$ hydrogenation from graph-based machine learning
items.summary: Dopants can tune the activity of zirconia-based CO$_2$ hydrogenation catalysts through changes in adsorbate and transition-state (TS) energetics. Computing these quantities with density functional theory (DFT) becomes expensive when several dopants, reaction intermediates, and TSs must be screened. Here, we further develop the graph-based machine learning method Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman Gaussian Process Regression (WWL-GPR): we introduce additional electronic-structure and local-environment features relevant for oxide surfaces and use the resulting model to predict adsorption and TS energies on ZrO$_2$(101) surfaces doped with Al$^{3+}$, Cd$^{2+}$, Ga$^{3+}$, In$^{3+}$, and Zn$^{2+}$. Adsorbate-surface structures are represented as attributed graphs that combine bonds connectivity and features. We benchmark WWL-GPR against thermodynamic scaling relations (TSR) for reaction intermediates and Bronsted-Evans-Polanyi relations (BEP) for TSs, and then propagate the predicted energies to microkinetic CH$_3$OH-yield estimates. WWL-GPR consistently improves the prediction of reaction intermediate energetics relative to linear scaling approaches and provides TS estimates that are competitive with BEP-based models. These improvements become especially relevant when the predicted energetics are propagated through the reaction network. Microkinetic calculations show that WWL-GPR-derived energies give CH$_3$OH yields closer to DFT-derived yields than the linear-relation workflow. Degree-of-rate-control analysis links the activity errors to dopant-dependent rate-controlling steps, including HCOO* formation, H$_2$COOH* dissociation, and H$_3$CO* formation. These results support WWL-GPR as a data-efficient surrogate for connecting atomistic energetics with catalyst-screening observables on doped oxide surfaces.

items.title: Geometric theory of elastic curves constrained on rigid curved surfaces
items.summary: Slender elastic objects constrained to curved surfaces are ubiquitous in soft systems, with examples ranging from DNA wrapping around histones to actin filaments forming contractile rings on the cell membrane during cytokinesis. In the continuum limit, the conformation of these effectively one-dimensional (1D) objects is governed by both the geometry and mechanics of the embedding surface, and the elasticity of the object. Existing phenomenological typically describe such behavior through elastic energy minimization that incorporates bending and twisting, but neglect stretching that may be important for filaments with finite cross-section or are highly incompatible with the underlying surface. Here we present a coarse-grained geometric theory of 1D elastic curves constrained on rigid surfaces, derived from the first principles. For an isotropic material, our model emerges naturally in terms of the Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and area moments of inertia. The resulting effective energy functional explicitly includes stretching in addition to bending and twisting. We minimize it to determine the equilibrium curve conformations on different zero, positive, or negative Gaussian rigid surfaces. Our theory provides a general framework for analyzing the equilibrium configurations of surface-bound elastic curves in biologically and physically relevant settings.

items.title: Locality-Preparation Time Tradeoffs in Dissipative Quantum Systems
items.summary: Dissipative state preparation engineers quantum many-body states as steady states of an open-system dynamics. The spatial range of the required dissipation sets both the feasibility of analog implementations and the connectivity and control complexity of digital ones. Yet how this locality quantitatively constrains preparation times remains largely unknown. Here, we establish an exact locality-preparation time relation for quadratic fermionic systems and develop a construction that optimizes the locality of the dissipative dynamics while preserving the target state. Applied to the Kitaev chain, our framework reveals sharply different locality-preparation time tradeoffs in critical and gapped regimes. At criticality, suppressing the algebraic tails of the jump operators necessarily forces the preparation time to grow algebraically with system size. By contrast, both trivial and topological gapped phases admit exponentially localized dissipation with a finite preparation time in the thermodynamic limit. Our results identify when fast dissipative preparation is compatible with local control and when criticality imposes an unavoidable dynamical cost.

items.title: Scalene Yang-Baxter triples realize all nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians with global additive symmetries
items.summary: We establish that bond Hamiltonian densities, up to local difference terms whose sum vanishes under periodic boundary conditions, lying in the commutant of bond operators, $w_j\pm w_{j+1}$, is a necessary and sufficient condition for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian to conserve a uniform or staggered sum of the one-site operators $w_j$. Starting from these local commutants, we show that every such Hamiltonian and its conserved charge can be obtained from monodromy matrices constructed using regular and non-regular members of scalene Yang-Baxter triples. The results hold on periodic chains of length $L\geq3$, with even length required in the staggered case. The results do not require translation invariance, and hence the interaction on each bond can be chosen independently from the full corresponding commutant. Our representation-independent construction applies in arbitrary finite local dimension and exhausts the Hamiltonians with either prescribed additive symmetry, without requiring ordinary Yang-Baxter integrability. We illustrate the construction with spin-$\tfrac12$ and spin-1 systems and discuss its relation to the double-commutant theorem. Classifying the one-site generators $w$ and their associated bond commutants provides a route to classifying such Hamiltonians with additive conserved charges.

items.title: Josephson junctions, superconducting circuits, and qubit for quantum technologies
items.summary: In the realm of physics, a pivotal moment occurred six decades ago when Brian Josephson made a groundbreaking prediction, setting in motion a series of events that would eventually earn him the prestigious Nobel Prize eleven years later. This prediction centered around what is now known as the Josephson effect, a phenomenon with far-reaching implications. At the heart of this effect lies the Josephson junction (JJ), a device that has become a linchpin in various scientific applications. This chapter delves into the foundational principles of the Josephson effect and the remarkable properties of JJs. From their role in metrology to their application in radiation detectors, these junctions have ushered in a new era of electronics. Exploiting the unique features of superconductive devices, such as high speed, low dissipation, and dispersion, JJs find today practical implementation in the development of superconductive qubits and nanotechnology applications.

items.title: Utilizing Neural Networks for Solving Functional Renormalization Group Flow Equations
items.summary: A novel physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based approach for solving functional renormalization group flow equations is presented. We investigate the finite temperature phase transition in $O(N)$ models without relying on the large-$N$ approximation, which was used in earlier attempts with similar methods. We argue that these previous solutions cannot easily be generalized for more complex symmetries, and hence our approach can provide new insight. Our technique relies on a series of ansätze that combines the small- and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, leading to a highly accurate approximation over the entire field range. We compare the PINNs approach with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results and show that the network can successfully learn the temperature, field, and scale dependencies of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.

items.title: Arrested phase separation and amorphous patterns in charged binary fluids
items.summary: Frustration generated by competing interactions can stabilise patterns with tunable lengthscales which evade indefinite coarsening and macroscopic phase separation. Here we investigate a charged binary fluid in which the tendency toward phase separation is opposed by screened electrostatic repulsion. Combining analytics and numerical simulations, we identify a regime of arrested phase separation characterised by finite-wavelength instability. The resulting states include droplet and labyrinthine phases in two dimensions, and droplets, concentric shells and tubular structures in three dimensions. Surprisingly, some of these structures are amorphous morphologies that emerge reproducibly from different initial conditions. Free-energy estimates suggest that these disordered structures may be thermodynamically stabilised by frustration, rather than being kinetically trapped. Our results identify a simple mechanism through which the competition between phase separation and screened electrostatics can generate equilibrium amorphous microphases with glassy features.

items.title: A Generalizable Machine Learning Framework for Half-Heusler Thermoelectrics
items.summary: Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful approach for accelerating the discovery of thermoelectric (TE) materials, yet many models suffer from limited generalizability. Here we present a robust ML framework for predicting the thermoelectric figure of merit (zT) in half-Heusler (hH) compounds, emphasizing prediction of previously unseen compositions. A principal component analysis (PCA)-based train/test splitting strategy is introduced to generate representative partitions of chemical space. Bayesian hyperparameter optimization is combined with correlation-based k-best feature selection for Random Forest, XGBoost, and Neural Network models, together with the interpretable SISSO symbolic-regression method. Relative to the full set of 118 input features, the optimized feature subsets reduce the test RMSE by 16-27%. SHAP and SISSO analyses identify temperature, A-site dopant concentration, and A-site heat of vaporization as the most important descriptors of zT. The framework is validated through prediction of previously unexplored compositions, recovery of literature-reported optimal zT values for established hH systems, and first-principles calculations for the new compounds CeCoBi and CeIrBi, which exhibit favorable electronic transport properties. The framework is further applied to high-throughput screening of the doped hH chemical space, covering about 2.46 million elemental substitution combinations across 631 thermodynamically screened parent matrices under stability constraints. This screening yields a concise set of promising candidates for future study. Overall, the work establishes a generalizable workflow for reliable data-driven thermoelectric materials discovery.

items.title: Shear-driven arrest of dip-coating film entrainment
items.summary: A plate withdrawn from a bath of partially wetting liquid entrains a film above a critical velocity. Here, we show that this critical threshold can be substantially increased by the presence of a laminar gas flow opposed to the plate velocity that exerts a tangential shear stress on the liquid-gas interface. Using two-phase immiscible Navier-Stokes simulations and confining the gas to a narrow channel, we derive a closed-form expression for the interfacial stress, which combined with lubrication theory relates the thickness of the film and the contact line velocity to the applied shear stress. As the gas velocity is increased, the film thins and the contact line velocity slows down, until the imposed shear overcomes the drag of the moving plate and entrainment is arrested. As in the quiescent case, the velocity mismatch between plate and contact line is independent of the plate velocity and is set by the applied shear alone. We find that one set of varying gas flow simulations, with constant critical plate velocity, therefore determines the critical gas flow for every smaller plate velocity.

items.title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
items.summary: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ and $Δ=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

items.title: Efficient simulation of second-order phase transitions in quantum anharmonic materials
items.summary: When a crystal undergoes a second-order structural phase transition, such as in ferroelectrics, Peierls, and charge-density waves, the diverging fluctuations of the order parameter lead to the break- down of the standard phonon quasiparticle picture. Simulating these highly anharmonic regimes is notoriously challenging, as methods such as molecular dynamics suffer from a critical slowdown near the transition point, while the harmonic approximation fails dramatically at saddle points of the energy landscape stabilized by quantum or thermal ionic fluctuations. This work introduces a new approach, based on the variational free-energy principle, to predict critical long-range behavior and dynamical spectra in strongly anharmonic systems, even when quantum ionic fluctuations dominate. The proposed framework builds upon the stochastic self- consistent harmonic approximation but reduces its computational scaling with the number of atoms, N, from O(N^6) to O(N^2) and the memory requirement from O(N^4) to O(N). We benchmark the method on the prototypical lead-free metal-halide perovskite CsSnI3, a promising candidate for photovoltaic engineering, simulating its phase stability and Raman spectrum near the phase transition, where the breakdown of the quasiparticle picture becomes evident. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the method by computing the full free-energy Hessian and the critical temperature in a supercell with 1080 atoms. Such simulations would have required tens of thousands of years with the legacy approach; it is now feasible in a few hours on consumer hardware.

items.title: Liouvillian interpolation of the self-energy of cluster dynamical mean-field theories
items.summary: Two widely-used non-local extensions of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), namely cellular DMFT (CDMFT) and the dynamical cluster approximation (DCA), both yield self-energies marred by having some unphysical properties: CDMFT yields real-space self-energies that are not translationally invariant, and DCA yields momentum-space self-energies with discontinuities in their momentum dependence. It is often desirable to remove these flaws by post-processing cluster DMFT results, using strategies called periodization for CDMFT and interpolation for DCA---for brevity, we refer to both cases as \textit{interpolation}. However, traditional interpolation approaches struggle to reliably capture intricate structures such as hole pockets in the hole-doped square-lattice Hubbard model. Further, these approaches interpolate frequency-dependent functions, which may lead to causality violations. Here, we propose \textit{Liouvillian interpolation}, a novel, intuitive, and robust scheme for interpolating cluster DMFT results. Our key idea is to interpolate frequency-\textit{independent} matrix elements of the single-particle irreducible part of the Liouvillian, obtained from a continued-fraction expansion of the cluster DMFT self-energy. We demonstrate that the ingredients of such an expansion possess a more local Fourier expansion than the functions involved in traditional interpolation schemes, and that Liouvillian interpolation conserves causality by construction. We illustrate our method for the one-dimensional Hubbard model using CDMFT, and for the two-dimensional Hubbard model using four-site CDMFT and four-patch DCA. For the latter, $\mathcal{L}$-interpolation can (depending on doping) yield Fermi and Luttinger arcs which together seem to form a closed surface.

items.title: Dislocation mediated twin boundary faceting in $β$-Sn
items.summary: Grain boundaries (GBs), including twin boundaries (TBs), play a critical role in plastic deformation by interacting with dislocations. The deformation and strengthening mechanisms in $β$-Sn are of significant interest because Sn-based alloys are widely used as solder materials. Recent experiments have shown deformation-induced faceting in $β$-Sn arising from twin-dislocation interactions. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations informed by a recently developed machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP), we demonstrate a $\langle c\rangle$ dislocation-absorption mediated faceting reaction along $(301)$ TBs in $β$-Sn in which facet length grows with the number of absorbed dislocations. We show that the predicted facet length is consistent with isotropic elasticity theory only when the disclination character of the asymmetric twin facet is taken into account. We discuss analogies to faceting reactions in other low symmetry metals and hypothesize that the ubiquity of $(301)$ twins in $β$-Sn stems from their ability to grow rapidly through a forest of dislocation obstacles.

items.title: Instabilities in self-consistent diagrammatic approaches and how to cure them
items.summary: While self-consistent diagrammatic approaches are widely used to compute the physical properties of correlated quantum materials, their applicability may get severely hindered precisely in the parameter regions where the most exciting physics is observed. One of the major issues, referred to as "misleading convergence", is the tendency of iterative schemes to converge to unphysical fixed points for intermediate-to-strong electronic interactions, regardless of the numerical accuracy of the computation. Here, we explicitly verify that the origin of this problem in several established self-consistent many-electron approaches, defined in the general diagrammatic framework of the boson-exchange formalism, resides exclusively in the stability condition of the respective iteration schemes, and not in an intrinsic breakdown of their self-consistent diagrammatic description. This insight enables a simple and general remedy, as recently proposed in Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016502 (2026): The redefinition of the iterative procedure, by inverting the unstable eigendirections of the Jacobian associated with the fixed point of the self-consistent algorithm. We illustrate the successful outcome of this procedure by means of systematic calculations performed on exactly solvable testbed models. Our results demonstrate that the physical fixed point of the diagrammatic schemes we considered can be stabilized, de facto, across the entire parameter range, including the most challenging nonperturbative/strong-coupling regimes.

items.title: A new approach to the Kondo effect: sophomore's dream function and Lee-Yang zeros
items.summary: We develop an analytical approach to the Kondo problem based on an effective partition function that generalizes the sophomore's dream integral. The Kondo crossover is represented as a passage through an approximately equidistant ladder of its Lee-Yang zeros in the complex plane, rather than as a singularity on the real axis. Summation over this ladder yields the Gamma function $Γ(α+ T_K/(2 πT))$ as the universal crossover backbone, where the offset $α=1/2$ is fixed by the Friedel sum rule. The Euler-Maclaurin expansion connects the discrete zero structure to the Nozieres Fermi-liquid theory through Bernoulli numbers. A two-cutoff formula provides a compact, essentially one-parameter description of the full crossover in terms of a temperature-space Fano lineshape which is a thermal average of the energy-space Fano resonance observed in STM. Drift corrections are treated. The approach extends to $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Coqblin-Schrieffer, underscreened and Anderson impurity models, and Kondo lattices.

items.title: Parametric Glassiness in Graphene-based Electronic Lévy Glass
items.summary: Complex disordered conductors can display highly structured and parameter-sensitive transport even in the absence of a thermodynamically stable glass phase. Overlap distributions originally developed for replica symmetry breaking (RSB) provide a useful diagnostic of this organization, provided that their interpretation is distinguished from the equilibrium Parisi construction. In this study, we report RSB-like overlap phenomenology and parametric mesoscopic glassiness in a graphene-based electronic Lévy glass, a device that mimics optical phenomena via electronic processes. By tuning the Fermi energy, we can control the number of propagating wave modes and observe reentrant changes from narrowly centered to broad or bimodal overlap distributions. The phenomenology is observed in both graphene-based and conventional two-dimensional electron-gas electronic Lévy glasses, indicating its generality. Sample-resolved overlap distributions show that the effect is intrinsic to each disorder landscape, whereas the normalized conductance variance shows that the growth of the absolute variance is mainly caused by the increasing mean conductance. We therefore interpret the overlap as a measure of correlation among hierarchically organized transport pathways and the reentrant behavior as evidence of pinning, parameter-induced reorganizations, and mesoscopic chaos in coherent transport.

items.title: Demonstration of on-chip all-optical switching of magnetization in integrated photonics
items.summary: Ultrafast all-optical magnetization switching (AOS) holds great promise for nextgeneration spintronic memory and hybrid spintronic-photonic systems. However, most implementations to date rely on bulky free-space optical setups, limiting scalability and practical integration. As a critical step toward integrated applications, we demonstrate single-pulse AOS within a silicon nitride (Si3N4) photonic integrated circuit. Using trains of femtosecond laser pulses guided through on-chip waveguides, we achieve deterministic toggle switching in a sub-micron out-of-plane Co/Gd Hall cross patterned directly atop the photonic waveguide. Electrical readout via the anomalous Hall effect reveals a switching contrast of up to 90% for 500 nm-wide devices. In larger Hall crosses, the contrast decreases and switching becomes stochastic, consistent with spatially non-uniform optical absorption as confirmed by finite-element simulations. This behavior is hypothetically attributed to domain wall relaxation and thermally assisted (de)pinning processes within partially switched regions. Our results highlight the critical role of device scaling in achieving robust on-chip AOS and establish a foundation for ultrafast, energy-efficient, and fully integrated spintronic-photonic platforms.

items.title: Encoding Matters: A Qubit-Efficient Reformulation for Quantum Resilient Routing
items.summary: Qubits are powerful computational resources because each additional qubit doubles the size of the accessible state space. This expressive power comes at a cost: adding qubits also increases circuit size, constraint overhead, and exposure to hardware noise. These limitations are especially critical for near-term quantum computers, making the number of qubits required to formulate a problem a central practical concern. In this work, we present a method for efficiently mapping logistics and routing problems onto qubits through structure-aware encoding reduction. We demonstrate the method on a benchmark problem of latency-resilient routing under dual-link failures. For this benchmark, the reduced formulation substantially lowers both the qubit count and the compiled circuit complexity while preserving the original optimization task. By running the reduced model on the same trapped-ion quantum computer as the benchmark, we obtain a 100X improvement in the success probability. This finding shows how careful problem formulation can make current quantum hardware substantially more effective for practical optimization.

items.title: Ferroelectric Domain-Wall Motion, Stability, and Frequency Responses under Different Screening-Charge Conservation Laws
items.summary: We analyze ferroelectric domain wall motion, shape, and internal structure arising from coupling between polarization and screening charge. Universal cases are organized by electrical boundary conditions, charge conservation and dynamics, and polarization free energy. We consider exposed surfaces, interfaces beneath a dielectric layer and top electrode, and interfaces with a blocking mixed ionic-electronic conductor. Screening occurs through local exchange, exchange with lateral transport, or strictly conserved redistribution. Analytical derivations and finite-depth calculations establish screening drag, velocity branches, and conditions for spatial instability. For an isolated wall joining differently compensated domains, strict surface conservation and zero far-field current exclude steady translation of the screening profile, while allowing transient displacement, finite-sample arrest, and charge-balanced structural changes. Conservation also constrains long-distance transport around a moving junction in an adjoining conductor. Large-field simulations in the top-electrode geometry reveal nonlinear corrugation, transfer toward longer wavelengths, and coupled polarization rotation. First-order polarization energetics allow two interphase fronts enclosing a paraelectric core; multiaxial polarization permits wall rotation and competing intermediate ferroelectric domains. A driven structural-screening reduction supports stable periodic behavior. Reduced-variable diagrams summarize motion and structural regimes, while BaTiO3 and BiFeO3 examples connect them to material thermodynamics. Small-signal analysis distinguishes displacement, polarization, and electrostatic response functions. These results provide a framework for wall dynamics and structural transitions under different driving and screening conditions.

items.title: Predicting the Final Stationary State of Sheared 2D Euler Fluids
items.summary: The Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instability is a fundamental signature of the natural world, manifesting in phenomena ranging from atmospheric clouds to the iconic turbulence of Jupiter's Great Red Spot. While the linear dynamics of this instability is well-understood, the ultimate fate of the fluid --- the final stationary state to which it relaxes --- remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we present a general non-equilibrium statistical mechanics framework that allows us to predict the asymptotic vorticity distribution of a sheared 2D Euler fluid. By constructing a self-consistent ansatz for the solution of the Vlasov equation, we determine the stationary stream function without explicitly solving the time-dependent Euler equations. We demonstrate that the relaxation leads to a population-inverted core, where high-energy states are fully occupied, surrounded by a tenuous halo of vortices in the lower-energy regions of configuration space. This result establishes the core-halo structure as a robust statistical consequence of the system's evolution, offering a universal framework for understanding the saturation of shear-induced turbulence in inviscid 2D fluids.

items.title: Some remarks on the connection between generative diffusion and optimal transport
items.summary: We discuss three simple connections between generative diffusion and optimal transport. First, the joint law of the data and of their Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noising is, at every time, the solution of an entropic optimal-transport problem, at a temperature set by the noise level. Backward diffusion can consequently be read as an annealing which gradually decreases the entropic regularization. Second, we study the speciation transition--how the modes of the data distribution emerge during generation--and compare how it happens in diffusion and flow matching with respect to optimal transport. Using Gaussian mixtures as high-dimensional example, we show that the dynamical instability through which diffusion and flow matching separate the modes becomes, for optimal transport, an exponentially thin boundary layer at the beginning of generation, which is rounded by entropic regularization. Third, considering a generic forward dynamics with a general confining potential, we show that the backward process driven by the score also satisfies a drift-based variational principle whose minimal cost is the entropy difference between initial and final distributions.

items.title: Altermagnetic Control of Charge-4e Superconductivity
items.summary: We present, to our knowledge, the first theoretical realization of an independent charge-4e phase in a two-dimensional classical array of conventional superconductors coupled through altermagnetic junctions. Tuning the altermagnetic splitting suppresses the leading single-pair tunneling harmonic while retaining strong double-pair coupling, producing a finite charge-4e region between staggered and uniform charge-2e states. Using the complete temperature-dependent microscopic Josephson spectrum, we find short-range ordinary pair correlations alongside algebraic coherence of pairs of Cooper pairs. Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless scaling and a half-flux response further identify the charge-4e phase. Our results establish altermagnetism as a microscopic means to select between ordinary and composite superconducting coherence.

items.title: Efficient Transport Networks through Edge Pruning by Relative Resistance
items.summary: Transport networks are key to living and engineered systems. How can transport networks adapt efficiently using only local rules, without a global objective or specific boundary conditions? Inspired by observations in biological transport networks, we adapt networks by subsequently pruning edges by relative resistance, thus removing edges whose resistance is higher than the resistance for routing flow through the rest of the network. We find that adaptation by such a local, boundary-condition-free measure of redundancy, set by topology alone, yields sparse, loop-rich, low-dissipation networks.

items.title: Giant geometric nonlinear transport in inhomogeneously strained Bi$_2$Se$_3$ single crystalline slabs
items.summary: Electrical transport in non-centrosymmetric materials exhibits a nonlinear conductivity tensor component that generates second-harmonic voltages in response to applied electric fields. Harnessing this effect is essential for developing zero-threshold electromagnetic energy harvesters and broadband frequency upconverters, both of which require maximizing the nonlinear responsivity. Here, we demonstrate that inhomogeneously strained macroscopic slabs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Se$_3$ achieve a record-high nonlinear responsivity of $10^4\,μ$m/V: a six orders of magnitude boost compared to its thin-film counterparts. We attribute this giant enhancement to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect, which is driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material. Notably, a similar geometric mechanism known as geometric nonlinear Hall was previously observed only in microscale-patterned structures. Our findings establish macroscopic strain engineering as a powerful route to enhance nonlinear transport, with immediate relevance to a broad class of layered systems, including transition metal dichalcogenides and moiré heterostructures.

items.title: Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals
items.summary: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-André model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-André transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-André transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.

items.title: How Fluctuations Control Chiral Symmetry Breaking in Reacting Mixtures of Chiral Molecules
items.summary: The pronounced chiral asymmetry of biomolecules is a defining feature of living systems, yet the mechanisms by which such asymmetry emerged remain unresolved. Chiral symmetry breaking may have occurred under prebiotic conditions in systems with sufficiently small molecular populations for intrinsic fluctuations to play an important role. Here, we investigate how finite-population fluctuations affect chiral-state selection, the characteristic time for symmetry breaking, and stochastic switching between chiral states in a system driven by autocatalysis and mutual antagonism. We determine how these dynamical processes scale with particle number and derive an analytical expression for the probability of selecting either chiral state as a function of the initial enantiomeric bias. We further calculate the mean selection time for different initial biases and show that, for weak mutual antagonism, fluctuations can induce transitions between opposite chiral states. These results characterize how finite-population fluctuations control both the emergence and stability of molecular chirality in autocatalytic chemical systems.

items.title: Physics-inspired Generative AI models via real hardware-based noisy quantum diffusion
items.summary: Quantum Diffusion Models (QDMs) are an emerging paradigm in Generative AI that aims to use quantum properties to improve the performances of their classical counterparts. However, existing algorithms are not easily scalable due to the limitations of near-term quantum devices. Following our previous work on QDMs, here we propose and implement two physics-inspired protocols. In the first, we use the formalism of quantum stochastic walks, showing that a specific interplay of quantum and classical dynamics in the forward process produces statistically more robust models generating sets of MNIST images with lower Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) than using totally classical dynamics. In the second approach, we realize an algorithm to generate images by exploiting the intrinsic noise of real IBM quantum hardware with only four qubits. Our work could be a starting point to pave the way for new scenarios for large-scale algorithms in quantum Generative AI, where quantum noise is neither mitigated nor corrected, but instead exploited as a useful resource.

items.title: Latin squares as a model of perfect mixing of high-entropy alloys
items.summary: The structure of high-entropy alloys, which include 5 or more components in equimolar proportions, is proposed to be described in the mathematical language of Latin squares. This model is fundamentally discrete and allows for a quantitative description of ideal mixing, in which any given alloy element is guaranteed not to have an identical element as its nearest neighbor. For the two-dimensional case, the model possesses four axes of translational symmetry, which makes it possible to tile the plane with a single Latin square and, based on the properties of this square, describe the properties of macroscopic material samples. The model makes it possible to make quantitative estimates of the suitability of a particular atomic structure (configuration) for implementation in a perfectly mixed high-entropy alloy with maximum mixing entropy. A condition has been obtained for acceptable fluctuations in the concentration of components at which the thermodynamic stability of the alloy is maintained. The possibility of identifying superstructures in high-entropy alloys based on group theory, as applied to the description and construction of Latin squares, is discussed. Based on the proposed model, the probability of forming a multicomponent alloy with ideal mixing is estimated. For a five-component alloy, this probability is no more than 2.6*10^{-10}.

items.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
items.summary: Semi-Markov networks provide a natural framework for describing stochastic transitions between coarse-grained states with non-exponential dwell times, with applications ranging from biophysics and neuroscience to epidemiology and finance. Here, it is shown that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph. These representations yield asymptotic results, including a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem to semi-Markov networks, in which the rate constants replaced by pseudo-rates given by the inverse mean sojourn time weighted by the exit probability through this channel, as well as the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short proof of the constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to show that weak ergodicity breaking occurs generically for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks.

items.title: The effects of non-stoichiometric lattice structure and secondary phase α-Fe2O3 on modifying the magnetic, electrical, and magneto-electric properties of Eu doped BaFe12O19 hexaferrite
items.summary: The Ba-atoms in BaFe12O19 were substituted by Eu-atoms to prepare the material of composition Ba1-xEuyFe12O19. The Eu atoms occupied at the sites of Fe atoms. The atomic ratio of Eu/Ba were varied from 0 to 0.33 to control the secondary phase (hematite) and M-type hexaferrite. Raman spectra provided complimentary support for a systematic increase of the hematite phase on increasing the Eu/Ba ratio. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy informed the presence of oxygen deficiency and surface defects, and charge state of Ba and Fe/Eu ions close to +2 and +3, respectively. The material showed direct optical transitions with band gap in the range of 2.25-3.09 eV. The increase of Eu/Ba ratio systematically increased the saturation magnetization from 84.44 emu g-1 to 57.68 emu g-1 at 3 K and 67.09 emu g-1 to 43.42 emu g-1 at 300 K, along with remarkable enhancement of the coercivity (914- 3656 Oe at 3 K and 1996-4862 Oe at 300 K). Electrical conductivity increased from 10-11-10-10 Sm-1 at 30 K to 10-5 -10-4 Sm-1 at 300 K. The electrical conductivity analysis reveals the Efros-Shklovsky-type variable-range hopping mechanism at the low-temperature region, whereas the Mott variable range hopping mechanism is applicable near to room temperature. The analysis of current-voltage characteristics provided electrode to sample interfacial barrier height of 0.27-0.74 eV. The material exhibited novel magneto-electronic properties (bi-stable electronic switching and its transformation in the temperature scale, magnetoresistance and magnetoelectric coupling) which are highly useful for spintronic devices. This work demonstrates that controlled Eu/Ba atomic ratio in the stoichiometric and non-stoichiometric lattice structure could be an effective strategy to widely tune the magnetic, optical and magneto-electronic properties in M-type Ba hexaferrite material.

items.title: A new device for live cell imaging of biological samples under in-plane shear
items.summary: The effect of mechanical stresses and deformations upon the behavior and properties of cells and tissues is a topic of paramount interest in the field of biophysics. Its understanding is essential for deepening our comprehension of cellular responses to environmental stimuli, with implications in fields ranging from embryogenesis to tumor development. For boosting the understanding in this field, it is important to develop devices for the application of simple deformations in order to probe the cellular response to the basic mechanical transformations. While a number of stretching devices have been developed, in-plane shearing deformation has been little investigated. Here, a new device is introduced that allows the application of homogeneous in-plane shear upon a cell monolayer while imaging the sample with a commercial optical microscope. A description of the faced experimental challenges is reported and a full characterization is presented. It is demonstrated the capability of the device to apply reproducible, controlled and homogeneous shear of both single cells and confluent cellular monolayers.

items.title: Controlling the Atomic Reconstruction in Twisted MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ with a Monolayer hBN Spacer
items.summary: Twisted van der Waals heterobilayers are a promising material platform for studying collective exciton many-body phenomena, but near-aligned structures often exhibit a local, anisotropic atomic reconstruction that compromises lateral homogeneity. The present study describes how atomic-scale rearrangement in adjacent regions of hBN-encapsulated, near-aligned MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers is controlled by the presence of a mono- or bilayer hBN spacer between the two monolayers. High-angle annular dark-field STEM directly resolves the atomic alignment in both layers and shows that the spacer suppresses the reconstruction and strongly increases the structural uniformity of the heterobilayers. 4D-STEM quantitatively maps local rotation, dilation, and heterostrain, revealing that the separated regions remain consistent with rigid moiré superlattice simulations, whereas without the spacer the structural parameters have two to three times broader distributions. By suppressing reconstruction, ultrathin hBN spacers therefore provide an effective route to enhance lattice homogeneity in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers targeting collective excitonic and optoelectronic phenomena.

items.title: Topologically quantized macroscopic attractor states in hydrated DNA
items.summary: Driven dissipative systems at ambient conditions typically exhibit continuous responses shaped by fluctuations and relaxation, with discrete macroscopic states arising only under specific dynamical constraints. Here, we report the emergence of discrete attractor states in a quasi-two-dimensional hydrated DNA sample under magnetic excitation. The transverse polarization voltage $V_{xy}$ displays telegraph switching between well-defined levels, indicating stochastic transitions between metastable macroscopic states. Statistical analysis of the voltage time series reveals bimodal distributions and strong Bayesian model selection in favor of multiple coexisting states. A phenomenological phase-field framework describes the observed metastability and switching in terms of a proposed collective $U(1)$ polarization phase. Within this interpretation, phase-slip dynamics and integer-labeled winding sectors provide a possible organizing principle for the discrete macroscopic response. The results suggest that macroscopic quantization can emerge in a classical system at ambient conditions as a consequence of dissipative dynamics constrained by phase topology.

items.title: Magnetic-field-induced detwinning of orientational domains in altermagnet $α$-MnTe: A single-crystal neutron diffraction study
items.summary: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, which makes them promising for future spintronic and magnonic applications, but their macroscopic responses can be strongly reduced by domain averaging. In hexagonal $α$-MnTe, three symmetry-related in-plane Néel-vector orientations and their time-reversal counterparts form six magnetic domain states, complicating both magnetic structure determination and measurements of the chiral magnon response. Using single-crystal neutron diffraction, we show that an in-plane field applied along the $[-1,1,0]$ direction produces a common magnetic domain orientation that saturates near $μ_0H=2$ T. A constrained refinement of 61 nuclear and magnetic reflections collected at 2 K and 2 T yields $\mathbf{M}\parallel[1,1,0]$, an ordered moment of $4.62(8)~μ_\mathrm{B}$ per Mn, and an orientational domain population at $r_A:r_B:r_C=0.97:0.03(5):0$ that is compatible with a nearly complete alignment of orientational domains. Furthermore, an abnormal behaviour in the temperature dependence of the selected reflections is observed in 60-88 K, its microscopic origin is discussed within the context of possible intrinsic piezomagnetic or magnetoelastic effects. Because unpolarized diffraction neither distinguishes domain repopulation from continuous Néel-vector rotation nor resolves time-reversal antiphase domains, the field-prepared state is a near-single-orientation state rather than a truly single-domain state.
